title: Canopy: 44 Track Jungle Adventure Music Pack
tagline: 44 jungle music tracks for any engine, MIDI and OGG. The band changes on the way in.
description:
Canopy is a 44 track jungle adventure music pack for any game engine: one expedition in six legs, in OGG and MIDI.

It ships 38 full looping pieces and 6 short cues, royalty free for commercial games, with four full tracks free on this page.

What is inside

44 tracks · OGG + editable MIDI · 1:20:00 of music · every loop at least 58 seconds

  • A whole expedition, in order: The Last Port, Up the River, The Canopy, The Ruins, The Lost Temple and The Way Out. Port town, shop, map room and camp; the river by day and by night; canopy, waterfall, rope bridge and a village in the trees; ruins, traps and a chase; the temple from its antechamber to its heart.
  • Fights for each part of the map: Battle on the River, Battle in the Canopy and Battle in the Ruins, plus The Jaguar and The Old One as bosses.
  • The band changes on the way in. Every instrument belongs to the expedition (trumpet, clarinet, steel guitar and strings) or to the jungle (marimba, kalimba, pan flute and ocarina). Counted from the notes in the MIDI, the jungle plays 0% of Leg I, 4% of Leg II, 55% of Leg III, 84% of Leg IV and 100% of Leg V. Leg I and Leg V have no instrument in common. Leg VI plays both.
  • Two mallet parts interlock: marimba and kalimba share one pattern, each striking only in the other's gaps, so they never strike together and between them fill every slot of the grid. They arrive in the last section of each piece in Leg III and play the whole loop by Leg V. Each has its own channel in the MIDI.
  • The percussion follows the same map: bass drum, snare and hi hat at the port, maracas on the river, congas and bongos in the canopy, wood blocks and hands alone in the ruins and the temple.
  • One river theme in all 44 tracks, with seven more cells for places and fights. 6 cues: Discovery, Trap Sprung, Treasure, Rest at Camp, Victory and Lost in the Jungle.

The theory and audio reports (788 and 510 checks, 0 failed) ship inside the download.

The map: who plays each part in each leg, the jungle's share of the notes, where the mallets play and which drums sound.

The interlock: bars drawn from the MIDI, with a strip showing who struck every slot of the grid.

The score sheet: all 44 tracks, from Canopy to Lost in the Jungle.

Works with

RPG Maker MV and MZ read the loop tags with no plugin. The Readme gives import steps for Godot 4 (followed in a blank Godot 4.7.2 project, all 44 files), Unity and GameMaker. Any engine that plays OGG can use the files, and the MIDI drops into any DAW.

Try it free

Four full tracks with their MIDI are free on this page: Base Camp, Battle in the Canopy, The Jaguar and The Heart of the Temple. Base Camp is every part the expedition's and The Heart of the Temple is every part the jungle's, on the same river theme. More free tracks from our other albums: Overture, the free sampler.

Licence and how it was made

Royalty free for commercial games, no credit required. Do not resell the tracks as music assets. Every track is composed in code and rendered through a General MIDI soundfont; the jungle band is a set of General MIDI programs chosen for a made up jungle, not the music of any real people or place. No generative audio model is used. The composition system and this page's art were made with AI tools, as the tags below say. No song and no traditional tune is quoted.

Versions

v1.0 (3 November 2026): first release, 44 tracks.

devlog.title: Canopy is out: a jungle expedition score where the band changes on the way in, 44 tracks
devlog.body:
Canopy is a 44 track music pack for a jungle adventure: The Last Port, Up the River, The Canopy, The Ruins, The Lost Temple and The Way Out, plus 6 short cues.

The idea. Every instrument on the record belongs to one of two bands. At the last port every part is the expedition's: trumpet, clarinet, steel guitar, strings. Up the river the jungle takes the colour part. In the canopy it also takes the pad, and two mallet parts arrive that strike only in each other's gaps. In the ruins everything but the lead is the jungle's. In the temple the expedition's instruments are gone, and on the way out both bands play together. One river theme runs through all of it, so a player can hear the same tune in a different band.

How it was checked. 788 theory checks and 510 audio checks, 0 failed, with the reports inside the download. The band map, the mallets, the drum sounds, the river theme in every track and the loop tags are measured again on the extracted download. The jungle plays 0% of the notes in Leg I and 100% in Leg V, and those two legs share no instrument. The loop step was followed in a blank Godot 4.7.2 project on all 44 files.

The OGG files are rendered through a General MIDI soundfont, and the jungle band is a set of General MIDI programs chosen for a made up jungle, not the music of any real people or place. Nobody here can hear them: the four free tracks on the page are how to judge the sound. No generative audio model is used. The composition system and the cover art were made with AI tools. No song and no traditional tune is quoted.
